title: Microwave Mug Pizza
summary: Make a single-serving pizza in a microwavable mug: combine flour, salt, baking powder and baking soda, stir, add milk and olive oil, mix into a batter, top with marinara, mozzarella and Italian herbs, then microwave for about 1 minute 20 seconds until risen and bubbling.
source: CaptainCook4D recipe text + task graph (Microwave Mug Pizza); mistake hints from train split

nodes.name: Add 1/8 teaspoon salt
nodes.instruction_novice: Measure an eighth of a teaspoon of salt and tip it into the mug. That's just a small pinch.
substeps: Find the 1/8 teaspoon measuring spoon, or use a tiny pinch.
Scoop salt and level it off.
Tip the salt into the mug.
nodes.end_state: A small amount of white salt grains sits in the bottom of the mug or on top of the dry ingredients.
nodes.view_hint: looking down into the mug and at the measuring spoon in hand

checks.question: Was the salt added to the mug using a small measuring spoon?
Are white grains visible inside the mug?

mistakes.description: Used a large measuring spoon, adding far too much salt.
mistakes.visual_cue: A full teaspoon or tablespoon of salt being tipped into the mug.
mistakes.correction: That's too much salt. You only need an eighth of a teaspoon, a tiny pinch. Start over with a fresh mug if it's already in.
mistakes.early_cue: A teaspoon or tablespoon-size measuring spoon dipping into the salt.

mistakes.description: Added sugar instead of salt.
mistakes.visual_cue: Spoon dipping into a sugar container or bag labeled sugar.
mistakes.correction: That looks like sugar. You want salt here, so check the container.
mistakes.early_cue: Hand reaching toward the sugar container.

nodes.name: Sprinkle Italian herbs
nodes.instruction_novice: Sprinkle a pinch of dried Italian herbs over the cheese in the mug.
substeps: Pick up the dried Italian herb jar.
Shake or pinch a small amount over the cheese.
Spread it lightly so it isn't all in one spot.
nodes.end_state: Small green flecks of dried herbs are scattered over the white cheese on top of the mug.
nodes.view_hint: looking straight down into the mug

checks.question: Are green herb flecks visible on top of the cheese?
Is the jar in hand a dried herb seasoning rather than another spice?

mistakes.description: Sprinkled a different spice such as cinnamon or chili flakes instead of Italian herbs.
mistakes.visual_cue: Brown or red powder or flakes on the cheese instead of green flecks.
mistakes.correction: That doesn't look like Italian herbs. Check the label, you want the green dried herb mix.
mistakes.early_cue: Hand reaching for a jar with brown or red contents.

mistakes.description: Dumped a thick layer of herbs over the top.
mistakes.visual_cue: Cheese almost completely hidden under a green layer.
mistakes.correction: That's a lot of herbs, just a light sprinkle is enough. Brush some off if you can.
mistakes.early_cue: Jar tipped with the lid fully open rather than using the shaker holes.

nodes.name: Take 1 tablespoon marinara sauce
nodes.instruction_novice: Scoop one tablespoon of marinara sauce out of the jar with your measuring spoon.
substeps: Open the marinara jar.
Dip the tablespoon measure in and fill it.
Lift it out and hold it over the mug.
nodes.end_state: A tablespoon measure full of red marinara sauce is held in hand, lifted out of the jar.
nodes.view_hint: looking at the sauce jar and the measuring spoon in hand

checks.question: Is a tablespoon filled with red sauce in hand?
Is the sauce being taken from a marinara or pizza sauce jar?

mistakes.description: Picked up ketchup or another red sauce instead of marinara.
mistakes.visual_cue: A squeeze bottle or jar labeled ketchup or salsa in hand.
mistakes.correction: That's not marinara. Look for the pasta or pizza sauce jar instead.
mistakes.early_cue: Hand reaching for a squeeze bottle rather than a sauce jar.

mistakes.description: Scooped a lot more than one tablespoon of sauce.
mistakes.visual_cue: A heaping serving spoon of sauce rather than a level tablespoon.
mistakes.correction: That's a bit much sauce for one mug. Level it to one tablespoon so the batter doesn't go soggy.
mistakes.early_cue: Large serving spoon dipped into the jar.

nodes.name: Spread sauce over the batter
nodes.instruction_novice: Drop the sauce onto the batter and gently spread it across the surface with the back of the spoon, leaving it sitting on top.
substeps: Tip the sauce onto the middle of the batter.
Use the back of the spoon to push it outward to the edges.
Keep it on the surface, don't stir it in.
nodes.end_state: A thin, even red layer of sauce covers the top of the pale batter in the mug.
nodes.view_hint: looking straight down into the mug

checks.question: Is the batter surface covered with a red layer of sauce?
Is the sauce sitting on top rather than mixed into the batter?

mistakes.description: Stirred the sauce into the batter instead of spreading it on top.
mistakes.visual_cue: Batter turning uniformly pink or orange with no distinct red layer.
mistakes.correction: Try not to stir the sauce in, it should stay on top like a pizza. Spread it gently with the back of the spoon.
mistakes.early_cue: Fork plunged deep into the batter with circular stirring after the sauce is added.

mistakes.description: Left the sauce as a blob in the center without spreading.
mistakes.visual_cue: A single red mound in the middle with pale batter visible around the edges.
mistakes.correction: Spread the sauce out to the edges so the whole top is covered.
mistakes.early_cue: Spoon pulled away immediately after dropping the sauce.

nodes.name: Microwave 1 min 20 s
nodes.instruction_novice: Put the mug in the microwave and cook it for one minute twenty seconds, until the batter rises and the cheese is bubbling. Let it cool a moment before eating.
substeps: Place the mug in the center of the microwave.
Set the time to 1 minute 20 seconds and start.
Watch for it to rise and the cheese to melt and bubble.
Carefully remove with a towel, it will be hot.
nodes.end_state: The mug sits in the microwave with the pizza risen near the rim, cheese melted and bubbling, and the microwave stopped.
nodes.view_hint: through the microwave door, then the top of the mug after removal

checks.question: Is the mug inside the microwave with the door closed and the timer running or finished?
Has the batter risen with melted, bubbling cheese on top?
Does the display show about 1:20 as the set time?

mistakes.description: Batter rose above the brim and spilled over the side of the mug.
mistakes.visual_cue: Batter or cheese running down the outside of the mug or pooled on the microwave plate.
mistakes.correction: It's overflowing. Stop the microwave, let it settle, and next time use a larger mug or microwave in shorter bursts.
mistakes.early_cue: Batter rising right up to the rim within the first 30 seconds.

mistakes.description: Microwaved before the toppings were added, or before the batter was mixed.
mistakes.visual_cue: Mug going into the microwave with pale batter and no red sauce or cheese on top.
mistakes.correction: Wait, the toppings aren't on yet. Take it out and add the sauce, cheese and herbs first.
mistakes.early_cue: Microwave door opened while the sauce jar and cheese are still untouched.

mistakes.description: Set the wrong time, cooking far too long or too short.
mistakes.visual_cue: Microwave display showing a time well off 1:20, such as 5:00 or 0:20.
mistakes.correction: Check the timer, you want one minute twenty seconds. Adjust it before you start.
mistakes.early_cue: Fingers pressing many digits on the keypad.

mistakes.description: Removed the mug before the batter had risen and the cheese melted.
mistakes.visual_cue: Pale, wet batter and unmelted shredded cheese when the mug is taken out.
mistakes.correction: It's not done yet, the cheese should be bubbling. Pop it back in for another 15 to 20 seconds.
mistakes.early_cue: Microwave door opened well before the timer ends.

nodes.name: Add 4 tablespoons flour
nodes.instruction_novice: Measure four level tablespoons of flour and add them to the mug. Add the flour before any liquids.
substeps: Pick up the tablespoon measuring spoon.
Scoop flour and level it with your finger or a knife.
Tip it into the mug and repeat until you have four.
Count out loud so you don't lose track.
nodes.end_state: The mug is roughly a quarter full of loose white flour.
nodes.view_hint: looking down into the mug while scooping from the flour container

checks.question: Is there a visible pile of white flour inside the mug?
Was the flour added using a tablespoon measure, four times?

mistakes.description: Flour added after the milk and olive oil are already in the mug.
mistakes.visual_cue: Liquid already visible in the mug as flour is tipped in.
mistakes.correction: The flour should go in before the wet ingredients. It's okay, just stir really well now to get rid of lumps.
mistakes.early_cue: Milk or oil container opened before the flour has been measured.

mistakes.description: Wrong number of tablespoons, for example three or five.
mistakes.visual_cue: Mug noticeably underfilled or overfilled with flour compared with a quarter mug.
mistakes.correction: Double-check your count, you need exactly four tablespoons of flour.
mistakes.early_cue: Scooping motion repeated fewer or more than four times.

mistakes.description: Heaped, unleveled tablespoons giving too much flour.
mistakes.visual_cue: Flour mounded high above the rim of the measuring spoon.
mistakes.correction: Level each spoonful off with a knife so you don't end up with a dry, doughy pizza.
mistakes.early_cue: Spoon lifted from the flour with a tall mound on it.

nodes.name: Add 1 tablespoon olive oil
nodes.instruction_novice: Measure one tablespoon of olive oil and pour it into the mug on top of the stirred flour mix.
substeps: Open the olive oil bottle.
Fill the tablespoon measure level to the top.
Pour it into the mug.
nodes.end_state: A yellow-green pool of oil sits on top of the dry mixture in the mug.
nodes.view_hint: looking at the tablespoon under the oil bottle and the mug opening

checks.question: Is oil visible on top of the flour mixture in the mug?
Was the oil measured with a tablespoon before pouring?

mistakes.description: Oil added before the flour was in the mug.
mistakes.visual_cue: Oil pooling in the bottom of a mug that has no flour in it.
mistakes.correction: The flour should go in first. Add the dry ingredients now and stir well so the oil mixes in.
mistakes.early_cue: Oil bottle opened while the flour container is untouched.

mistakes.description: Poured oil straight from the bottle without measuring, adding too much.
mistakes.visual_cue: Bottle tipped directly over the mug with a long glug of oil.
mistakes.correction: Measure the oil with a tablespoon instead of pouring straight in, or the batter will be greasy.
mistakes.early_cue: Bottle lifted over the mug with no measuring spoon in the other hand.

nodes.name: Add 1/16 teaspoon baking soda
nodes.instruction_novice: Measure a sixteenth of a teaspoon of baking soda and tip it into the mug. That's about half of the smallest measuring spoon, just a tiny pinch.
substeps: Open the baking soda container.
Fill the 1/8 teaspoon spoon half way, or use a tiny pinch.
Tip it into the mug on top of the other dry ingredients.
nodes.end_state: A tiny pinch of fine white powder has been added to the dry ingredients in the mug.
nodes.view_hint: looking at the baking soda container and the mug opening

checks.question: Is the container being used labeled baking soda?
checks.roi: label on the container in hand

checks.question: Was only a very small amount tipped into the mug?

mistakes.description: Confused baking soda with baking powder, or added both from the same container.
mistakes.visual_cue: Spoon dipping into a container labeled baking powder during this step.
mistakes.correction: Check the label, that one is baking powder. You need the baking soda now, just a tiny pinch.
mistakes.early_cue: Hand reaching for the baking powder container.

mistakes.description: Added too much baking soda, giving a soapy taste.
mistakes.visual_cue: A full spoon of baking soda going into the mug.
mistakes.correction: That's a lot of baking soda. You only want a sixteenth of a teaspoon, so scoop a little out.
mistakes.early_cue: Measuring spoon filled heaping with baking soda.

nodes.name: Take a microwavable mug
nodes.instruction_novice: Grab a microwave-safe mug and set it on the counter in front of you. Pick a bigger one if you can, so the batter has room to rise.
substeps: Open the cupboard and pick a ceramic or glass mug with no metal trim.
Check it is empty and clean inside.
Set it upright on the counter within reach of your ingredients.
nodes.end_state: An empty, clean mug stands upright on the counter with its opening facing up.
nodes.view_hint: the counter in front of you, looking down into the mug

checks.question: Is there an empty mug standing upright on the counter?
Is the mug free of metallic rims or decorations?
checks.roi: rim and outside of the mug

mistakes.description: Picked a mug with a metallic rim or metal paint, which is not microwave safe.
mistakes.visual_cue: Shiny gold or silver band or lettering on the mug.
mistakes.correction: That mug has metal on it, so it can't go in the microwave. Swap it for a plain ceramic one.
mistakes.early_cue: Hand reaching for a mug with a shiny metallic band.

mistakes.description: Chose a very small mug, so the batter will overflow when it rises.
mistakes.visual_cue: An espresso-size or small cup on the counter instead of a standard mug.
mistakes.correction: That cup is a bit small. Grab a regular or large mug so the pizza has room to rise.
mistakes.early_cue: Hand picking up a small cup from the cupboard.

nodes.name: Mix into a batter
nodes.instruction_novice: Mix everything in the mug thoroughly with a fork until it becomes a thick batter. A few small lumps are fine.
substeps: Push the fork to the bottom and stir in circles.
Scrape the sides to pull in any dry flour.
Stop when no dry pockets remain, even if a few lumps are left.
nodes.end_state: The mug holds a thick, pale, smooth-ish batter with no dry flour visible on the sides or bottom.
nodes.view_hint: looking down into the mug while mixing

checks.question: Does the mug contain a thick wet batter with no dry flour pockets?
checks.roi: batter surface and sides of mug

checks.question: Is the batter mostly uniform in color?

mistakes.description: Mixed before the flour was added, so there is nothing to form a batter.
mistakes.visual_cue: Stirring a mug containing only liquid or only a thin paste while the flour is untouched.
mistakes.correction: The flour isn't in yet. Add the four tablespoons of flour and then mix it all together.
mistakes.early_cue: Flour container still closed when the wet ingredients are in the mug.

mistakes.description: Stopped mixing too soon, leaving dry flour stuck to the bottom and sides.
mistakes.visual_cue: White dry streaks visible along the inside wall or a dry layer at the bottom of the mug.
mistakes.correction: There's still dry flour on the sides. Scrape it in and keep mixing until it's all wet.
mistakes.early_cue: Fork lifted out after only a few turns.

nodes.name: Stir the dry ingredients
nodes.instruction_novice: Use a fork or spoon to stir the dry ingredients in the mug until the salt, baking powder and baking soda are mixed evenly into the flour.
substeps: Put a fork or small spoon into the mug.
Stir in circles, scraping the bottom and sides.
Keep going until the powders look evenly blended.
nodes.end_state: The flour mixture in the mug looks uniform with no separate clumps of powder, and a fork or spoon rests in or beside the mug.
nodes.view_hint: looking down into the mug while stirring

checks.question: Is a fork or spoon stirring inside the mug?
Do the dry ingredients look evenly blended with no separate piles?

mistakes.description: Stirred before all the dry ingredients were added to the mug.
mistakes.visual_cue: Stirring an empty or nearly empty mug, or stirring while flour or leavening containers are still untouched.
mistakes.correction: Hold on, not everything is in yet. Add the rest of the dry ingredients first, then stir.
mistakes.early_cue: Picking up a fork while the flour or baking powder is still unopened.

mistakes.description: Stirred only briefly, leaving clumps of salt or leavening in one spot.
mistakes.visual_cue: Visible separate white patches or granules on top of the flour after stirring stops.
mistakes.correction: Give it a few more stirs so the salt and baking powder are spread through the flour.
mistakes.early_cue: Fork lifted out of the mug after only one or two turns.

mistakes.description: Stirred so vigorously that flour spilled over the rim.
mistakes.visual_cue: Flour dust scattered on the counter around the mug.
mistakes.correction: Stir a little more gently so you don't lose flour over the side.
mistakes.early_cue: Fast, wide stirring strokes with flour puffing up.

nodes.name: Sprinkle mozzarella on the sauce
nodes.instruction_novice: Sprinkle a generous tablespoon of shredded mozzarella evenly over the sauce.
substeps: Grab a generous tablespoon of shredded mozzarella.
Sprinkle it over the sauce from side to side.
Make sure the cheese covers most of the red surface.
nodes.end_state: White shredded cheese covers most of the red sauce layer on top of the batter.
nodes.view_hint: looking straight down into the mug

checks.question: Is shredded white cheese visible on top of the sauce?
Does the cheese cover most of the sauce surface?

mistakes.description: Added the cheese before the sauce was spread, so cheese sits directly on the batter.
mistakes.visual_cue: White cheese on pale batter with no red sauce layer underneath.
mistakes.correction: The sauce goes on before the cheese. Lift off what cheese you can, spread the sauce, then add the cheese back.
mistakes.early_cue: Reaching for the cheese bag while the sauce jar is still closed.

mistakes.description: Only a few shreds of cheese added, leaving most of the sauce bare.
mistakes.visual_cue: Mostly red surface with scattered white strands.
mistakes.correction: Add a bit more cheese, you want a generous tablespoon covering the sauce.
mistakes.early_cue: Fingers pinching a very small amount from the bag.

nodes.name: Add 1/8 teaspoon baking powder
nodes.instruction_novice: Measure an eighth of a teaspoon of baking powder and add it to the mug. This helps the pizza rise.
substeps: Open the baking powder container.
Fill and level the 1/8 teaspoon spoon.
Tip it into the mug with the other dry ingredients.
nodes.end_state: A small level spoonful of white baking powder has joined the dry ingredients in the mug.
nodes.view_hint: looking at the baking powder container label and the mug opening

checks.question: Is the container being used labeled baking powder?
checks.roi: label on the container in hand

checks.question: Has a small spoonful of powder been tipped into the mug?

mistakes.description: Used baking soda instead of baking powder.
mistakes.visual_cue: Spoon dipping into a container labeled baking soda during this step.
mistakes.correction: That's the baking soda. For this step you want baking powder, an eighth of a teaspoon.
mistakes.early_cue: Hand reaching for the baking soda box.

mistakes.description: Skipped the baking powder, so the pizza will not rise.
mistakes.visual_cue: Moving on to stirring without the baking powder container ever being opened.
mistakes.correction: Don't forget the baking powder, an eighth of a teaspoon, or the base will stay flat.
mistakes.early_cue: Reaching for the spoon to stir while the baking powder is still closed.

nodes.name: Add 3 tablespoons milk
nodes.instruction_novice: Measure three tablespoons of milk and pour them into the mug on top of the flour mixture.
substeps: Open the milk.
Fill the tablespoon measure and pour it into the mug.
Repeat two more times, counting to three.
nodes.end_state: White milk is pooled over the flour and oil in the mug, starting to soak into the dry mix.
nodes.view_hint: looking at the tablespoon being filled and the mug opening

checks.question: Is liquid milk visible on top of the mixture in the mug?
Was the milk measured with a tablespoon rather than poured freely?

mistakes.description: Milk added before the flour was in the mug.
mistakes.visual_cue: Milk sitting in a mug with no flour in it.
mistakes.correction: Flour goes in before the milk. Add the dry ingredients now and mix well to avoid lumps.
mistakes.early_cue: Milk carton opened while the flour is still untouched.

mistakes.description: Poured milk directly from the carton, adding far more than three tablespoons.
mistakes.visual_cue: Carton tipped over the mug with the mixture turning soupy and thin.
mistakes.correction: That's too much milk, the batter should be thick. Measure three tablespoons next time, and add a little more flour to thicken it.
mistakes.early_cue: Carton lifted over the mug with no measuring spoon.
